paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: The image displays a donut chart with two concentric rings, illustrating the distribution of samples (%) across different values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity Std (Outer)", is divided into four segments, each corresponding to a standard deviation value: Std: 0.0 (dark blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (medium blue, 7.0%), Std: 0.82 (bright blue, 5.0%), and Std: 0.94 (light blue, 39.0%). The inner ring, labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)", is segmented into three parts: Max: 1 (light blue, 47.7%), Max: 2 (very light blue, 14.2%), and Max: 3 (pale blue, 38.0%). Each segment is labeled with its percentage value, and the legend on the right side of the chart provides the color coding for both the outer and inner rings. The chart visually represents how samples are distributed across these two metrics of ambiguity, with the outer ring showing the standard deviation levels and the inner ring showing the maximum ambiguity levels, allowing for a comparative view of the data distribution.
